Rashi on Shabbat 17b:1:1.english: Tavi - The name of the man.

Rashi on Shabbat 17b:1:2.english: Rishba - One who spreads nets to hunt wild animals and birds.

Rashi on Shabbat 17b:1:3.hebrew: גידולי תרומה - אם זרעה, ואפי' דבר שזרעו כלה, כגון תבואה וקטנית:
Rashi on Shabbat 17b:1:3.english: Growths of teruma - If [one] sowed it, and even [in the case of] an item whose seed disintegrates, such as grain and legumes.

Rashi on Shabbat 17b:1:4.hebrew: תרומה טהורה ביד ישראל - ועינו צרה ליתנה לכהן, וזורעה לבטלה מתורת תרומה:
Rashi on Shabbat 17b:1:4.english: Pure teruma in the hand of an Israelite - And he begrudges giving it to a priest, and sows it to nullify its status as teruma.

Rashi on Shabbat 17b:2:1.hebrew: אי דחשידי להכי אפרושי נמי לא ליפרשו - אלא חטה אחת מן הכרי כדשמואל. ומדאפרשו, ש"מ לא חשידי:
Rashi on Shabbat 17b:2:1.english: If they are suspected of that, let them not separate either - Except for one grain of wheat from the pile, in accordance with [the opinion of] Shmuel. And since they separated, learn from this that they are not suspected.

Rashi on Shabbat 17b:2:2.hebrew: משום תרומה טמאה ביד כהן - שאסורה באכילה, ובא לזורעה, וגזור שתהא בשמה הראשון, והרי היא תרומה טמאה — דחיישינן דילמא משהי לה עד זמן זריעה, ואתי למיכל בטומאתה:
Rashi on Shabbat 17b:2:2.english: Due to impure teruma in the hand of a priest - Which is forbidden to be eaten, and [the priest] comes to sow it; and [the Sages] decreed that [the growth] retain its original status, and behold, it is impure teruma — for we are concerned lest he keep it until the sowing season, and come to eat it in its [state of] impurity.

Rashi on Shabbat 17b:3:1.hebrew: נותן כיסו לנכרי - ולא יטלטלנו פחות פחות מד' אמות:
Rashi on Shabbat 17b:3:1.english: He gives his purse to a gentile - And he may not carry it in increments of less than four cubits.

Rashi on Shabbat 17b:4:1.english: Of Sanvata - [This is the] name of a place.

Rashi on Shabbat 17b:4:2.hebrew: ובנותיהן - במס' ע"ז פרכינן: בנותיהן דאורייתא נינהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 17b:4:2.english: And their daughters - In Tractate Avodah Zarah we raise the objection: Aren't their daughters [forbidden] by Torah law?

Rashi on Shabbat 17b:4:3.hebrew: כולן מי"ח דברים הן - והא כולהו חדא היא, דגזרו על פיתן משום שמנן, ועל שמנן כו', כדלקמן:
Rashi on Shabbat 17b:4:3.english: All of them are of the eighteen matters - And behold, all of them are [considered] one [decree], for they decreed upon their bread because of their oil, and upon their oil, etc., as [explained] below.

Rashi on Shabbat 17b:4:4.hebrew: הניחא לר"מ - דמנו להו להא דמניח כלים תחת הצינור, הוו להו י"ח: ט' דפסלי תרומה, ואין קורין, ואין פולין — הא חדסר. פשו להו ז': צינור, ומרדע, ובנות כותים, ובוצר, וגידולי תרומה, ונותן כיסו, ופיתן ושמנן — חדא:
Rashi on Shabbat 17b:4:4.english: This works out well according to Rabbi Meir - Since they count that [decree] of one who places vessels under the gutter pipe, they are eighteen: nine that disqualify *teruma*, and 'one may not read [by the light of a lamp],' and 'one may not search [one's clothes for lice]' — that is eleven. There remain seven: [the gutter] pipe, and the [ox] goad, and the daughters of Samaritans, and one who harvests [grapes for the winepress], and the growth of *teruma*, and one who gives his purse [to a gentile], and their bread and their oil [counted as] one.

Rashi on Shabbat 17b:4:5.hebrew: איכא הא - דמוסיף רב יצחק אדאבימי, על דבר אחר משום ד"א:
Rashi on Shabbat 17b:4:5.english: There is that [statement] - For Rav Yitzḥak adds onto [the statement of] Avimi: "[A decree] on something else because of something else."

Rashi on Shabbat 17b:5:1.hebrew: ועל בנותיהן משום ד"א - ע"ז. ועוד גזרו על ד"א שלא הוזכר כאן:
Rashi on Shabbat 17b:5:1.english: And upon their daughters due to something else - [That is,] idolatry. And furthermore, they decreed upon "something else" that was not mentioned here.

Rashi on Shabbat 17b:5:2.english: That he transmits impurity through zivah - And even if he is not a zav.

Rashi on Shabbat 17b:5:3.hebrew: אוכלין וכלים שנטמאו במשקין - חדא חשיב להו:
Rashi on Shabbat 17b:5:3.english: Food and vessels that became impure through liquids - [Rabbi Meir] counts them as one.

Rashi on Shabbat 17b:6:2.hebrew: כרשינין - למאכל בהמה, בינ"א בלע"ז:
Rashi on Shabbat 17b:6:2.english: Vetch - For animal food; veces [vetch] in Old French.

Rashi on Shabbat 17b:6:3.hebrew: וב"ה מתירין - משנתן את המים מבעוד יום:
Rashi on Shabbat 17b:6:3.english: And Beit Hillel permit - Once he has put the water [in] while it is still day.

Rashi on Shabbat 17b:6:4.hebrew: אונין - ארישב"א, והן אגודות של פשתן מנופץ, ונותנין אותו בקדרה לתנור, ומתלבן:
Rashi on Shabbat 17b:6:4.english: Bundles - [Old French: *ristes*] — and they are bundles of combed flax; and one places it in a pot into the oven, and it is bleached.

Rashi on Shabbat 17b:6:5.english: That they will steam - That they will become heated.

Rashi on Shabbat 17b:6:6.english: The eye - The dye, [meaning] that [the wool] absorb [it] while it is still day.

Rashi on Shabbat 17b:6:7.hebrew: מתירין - לתתה מבעו"י, והיא קולטת כל הלילה:
Rashi on Shabbat 17b:6:7.english: [Beit Hillel] permit - To place it [into the kettle] while it is still day, and it absorbs [the dye] all night.

Rashi on Shabbat 17b:7:1.english: Nor may one load with him - Onto the donkey.

Rashi on Shabbat 17b:7:2.hebrew: ולא מגביהין עליו - משאוי על כתיפו, דנראה כמסייעו להוליך בשבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 17b:7:2.english: Nor do they lift onto him - A burden onto his shoulder, for it appears as though he is assisting him to carry [it] on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 17b:7:3.hebrew: אלא כדי שיגיע למקום קרוב - כלומר, שיהא המקום קרוב שיוליכנו שם מבעו"י:
Rashi on Shabbat 17b:7:3.english: Unless [there is sufficient time] for him to reach a nearby place - That is to say, that the place must be close [enough] for him to bring it there while it is still day.

Tosafot on Shabbat 17b:2:1.hebrew: כיון דאפשר למיעבד כשמואל מהימני - הקשה ריב"א: תרומת מעשר, דלא אפשר להו למיעבד כשמואל — ליגזור? ותירץ ר"י: דמ"מ אמת הוא שגזרו אף על גידולי תרומה גדולה, ורוצה לפרש טעם בכולן. ומהר"ם אמר: דתרומת מעשר — מהימני הלוים, דאין נותנין מעשר אלא לחברים. וריב"א תירץ: דאותן שהיו חשודים — לא היו מפרישין כלל, כדאמ' בסוטה; וחברים שהיו מפרישים — מהימני [תוס ישנים]:
Tosafot on Shabbat 17b:2:1.english: "Since it is possible to act in accordance with Shmuel, they are trusted" - Riba raised a difficulty: [Regarding] terumat ma'aser, where it is not possible for them to act in accordance with [the opinion of] Shmuel — let [the Sages] decree [due to pure terumat ma'aser in the hand of a Levite]! And the Ri answered that nevertheless, it is true that they decreed even on the growths of teruma gedolah, and [the Gemara] wants to explain the reason for all of them. And the Maharam said that [with regard to] terumat ma'aser, the Levites are trusted, as one gives tithes only to chaverim. And Riba answered that those who were suspect would not separate [tithes] at all, as we say in Sotah; and the chaverim who did separate are trusted. [Tosafot Yeshanim]

Tosafot on Shabbat 17b:2:2.hebrew: דילמא משהי ליה גביה ואתי ביה לידי תקלה - פי' בקונטרס, ולכך גזרו דאפי' יזרענה דהוי טמאה. וקשה לר"י, דאמר בהדיא בפרק כל שעה (פסח. ם דף לד. ושם): "שתילי תרומה טמאה טהורים מלטמא ואסורין מלאכול" — פי': לזרים, כדמפרש התם — אלמא לכהנים שרי! וי"ל: כיון דאין נאכלין לזרים, משום ריוח פורתא שמטהרין לא משהי גביה. והא דהכא חיישינן לתקלה, ובספ"ק דפסחים (דף כ:) אמרי ב"ה "תעשה זילוף" — איכא למימר: דהכא מודו ב"ה, דפעמים שצריך להשהות שנה שלימה עד זמן זריעה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 17b:2:2.english: "Lest he keep it with him and come thereby to a stumbling block" - [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres, and therefore [the Sages] decreed that even if he sows it, it remains impure. And the Ri finds it difficult, for it states explicitly in the chapter [entitled] Kol Sha'ah (Pesachim 34a and ibid.): "Saplings of impure teruma [that were planted] are pure from imparting impurity, but are forbidden to be eaten" — meaning, [forbidden] to non-priests, as is explained there — thus, for priests it is permitted! And one can say: Since they cannot be eaten by non-priests, for the sake of the slight gain that they become pure, he will not keep [the produce] with him. And as for the fact that here we are concerned about a stumbling block, whereas at the end of the first chapter of Pesachim (20b) Beit Hillel say, "It may be used for sprinkling" — it can be said: Here Beit Hillel concede, as at times one must keep it for a whole year until the sowing season.

Tosafot on Shabbat 17b:4:1.hebrew: הניחא לר' מאיר אלא לרבי יוסי שבסרי הויין - ה"מ נמי למימר: אלא לר' טרפון, מאי איכא למימ'? רש"י חשיב "אין פולין" ו"אין קורין" בתרתי, וכן משמע מדקתני בברייתא: "אלו מן ההלכות", ולא קתני בברייתא אלא הנהו תרתי. והא דלא חשיב מבחין בין בגדו לבגדי אשתו ושמש הבודק כוסות וקערות לאור הנר — הנך נפקו מכלל הני תרתי, שהן עיקר. מיהו קשה, דלא מני רש"י הך ד"לא יאכל הזב עם הזבה", דודאי מי"ח דבר הוה, דקתני לה במתניתין בהדיא! ולפי זה, אוכל ראשון ואוכל שני — חדא חשיב להו; א"נ: "הבא ראשו ורובו במים שאובין" ו"טהור שנפלו כו'" חשיב חדא, משום דאי לא הא — לא קיימא הא, כי היכי ד"פתן ושמנן ויינן ובנותיהן" חשיב גזירה אחת. וההיא ד"לא יאכל זב פרוש עם זב עם הארץ", דקתני עלה בתוספתא: "אלו מן ההלכות", איכא למימר דהוי בכלל "לא יאכל הזב עם הזבה":
Tosafot on Shabbat 17b:4:1.english: This works out well according to Rabbi Meir, but according to Rabbi Yosei they are seventeen - [The Gemara] could also have said: "Rather, according to Rabbi Tarfon, what is there to say?" Rashi counts [the decrees of] "one does not search [for lice]" and "one does not read" as two [separate decrees], and this is also indicated by the fact that it is taught in a baraita: "These are among the halakhot," and the baraita only teaches those two. And as for the fact that [Rashi] does not count [the prohibitions against] distinguishing between his garment and his wife's garments, and a servant inspecting cups and dishes by the light of the lamp — these were derived from the general principle of those two, which are primary. However, it is difficult that Rashi did not count that [decree] that "a zav may not eat with a zavah," which certainly was [one] of the eighteen matters, as [the Mishnah] teaches it explicitly! And according to this, [one who eats] food [with impurity] of the first degree and food of the second degree are counted as one [decree]. Alternatively, "one who places his head and the greater part of his body into drawn water" and "a pure person upon [whose head and the greater part of his body three log of drawn water] fell, etc.," are counted as one, because if not for the one, the other would not stand — just as "their bread, their oil, their wine, and their daughters" is counted as one decree. And that [ruling] that an abstinent zav may not eat with an am ha'aretz zav, regarding which it is taught in the Tosefta, "These are among the halakhot," one can say that it is subsumed under "a zav may not eat with a zavah."

Tosafot on Shabbat 17b:5:1.hebrew: על פתן ושמנן משום יינן - הקשה ריב"א: מ"ש שהחמירו טפי ביין לאסור בהנאה מפת ושמן? ותירץ: מפני שהיין משמח אלהים ואנשים, והיו רגילין לנסכו אפי' שלא בפני ע"ז — הואיל והוצרכו לאוסרו משום בנותיהם, נתנו בו חכמים דין וחומר יין נסך ממש, כיון דפעמים היו מנסכין אותו אפי' שלא בפני ע"ז:
Tosafot on Shabbat 17b:5:1.english: "On their bread and their oil due to their wine" - Riba raised a difficulty: Why is [wine] different, that they were more stringent regarding wine to prohibit [even deriving] benefit [from it], more than [with regard to] bread and oil? And he answered: Because wine "gladdens God and man," and they were accustomed to pour it as a libation even not in the presence of an idol — [therefore,] since [the Sages] needed to prohibit it on account of their daughters, the Sages gave it the legal status and stringency of actual libation wine, since at times they would pour it as a libation even not in the presence of an idol.

Tosafot on Shabbat 17b:5:2.hebrew: ועל בנותיהם משום דבר אחר - ואם תאמר: הניחא למ"ד דמפרש בפרק ב' דמסכתא ע"ז (דף לו:) דעל בנותיהם גזרו יחוד — דשייך למיגזר משום ע"ז; אלא למ"ד דעל בנותיהם גזרו נדות — מה שייך הך גזירה לע"ז? וי"ל: דע"י שגזרו עליהם נדות, יפרשו ממגען ולא יטמעו בהם כ"כ:
Tosafot on Shabbat 17b:5:2.english: "And on their daughters due to something else" - And if you say: Granted according to the one who explains in the second chapter of Tractate Avodah Zarah (36b) that regarding their daughters they decreed [a prohibition against] seclusion — as it is relevant to decree [this] because of idolatry; but according to the one who says that regarding their daughters they decreed [the status of] niddah — what relevance does this decree have to idolatry? And one can say: Because they decreed [the status of] niddah upon them, [Israelites] would separate from contact with them and would not assimilate among them so much.

Tosafot on Shabbat 17b:6:1.hebrew: אונין - פי' בקונ': נותנים בתנור ומתלבן. וכן משמע בפ"ב (דף כז:), דאמרי': "האונין של פשתן משיתלבנו":
Tosafot on Shabbat 17b:6:1.english: Bundles - [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres: [One] places [them] into the oven and [the flax] is bleached. And so it is implied in the second chapter (27b), where we say: "Bundles of flax, once they are bleached."

Tosafot on Shabbat 17b:7:1.hebrew: אין פורסין מצודות כו' - אע"ג דבשבת נמי, אם פירש מצודה אינו חייב חטאת, שאינו יודע אם יצוד אם לאו — מ"מ גזרו לפרוש מצודה, דפעמים אתי לידי חיוב חטאת, כגון שבשעת פריסתו ילכוד; דהכי קתני בתוספתא: הפורס מצודה לבהמה או לעוף ונכנס לתוכה — חייב:
Tosafot on Shabbat 17b:7:1.english: "One may not spread traps, etc." - Even though on Shabbat as well, if one spread a trap he is not liable for a sin-offering, since he does not know whether it will trap [anything] or not, nevertheless they decreed [against] spreading a trap, because at times it may lead to liability for a sin-offering — such as where at the time of his spreading [it], he captures [an animal]. For so it is taught in the Tosefta: "One who spreads a trap for an animal or for a bird, and it enters into it, is liable."

Tosafot on Shabbat 17b:7:2.hebrew: אלא בכדי שיצודו - וא"ת: מנא ידע מתי יבא החיה? וי"ל: דבירושלמי מוקי לה בפורש בחורשין, דמצוין שם חיותא. ומיירי בענין זה שלא יוכל ללכוד במצודה אלא א' או ב', דהא מה מועיל שיצודו מבעוד יום, אם יכול לצוד גם משחשכה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 17b:7:2.english: "Only [if there is sufficient time] for them to be trapped" - And if you say: How does he know when the animal will come? And one can say: In the Yerushalmi, [the Gemara] establishes it [as referring to] one who sets [traps] in thickets, where animals are commonly found. And it is dealing with such a case where [the trap] cannot catch in the trap more than one or two [animals], for what does it avail that they are trapped while it is still day, if it can also trap after dark?

Tosafot on Shabbat 17b:7:3.hebrew: אין מוכרים לנכרי - אף על גב דאי עביד להו בשבת לא מיחייב חטאת, מ"מ מאחר שהנכרי מחמר או עושה בשבת בידים דבר שישראל אסור מן התורה — גזרו רבנן עם חשכה, כדפירש בקונטרס, משום דמיחלף בשלוחו. אבל בהנך דברים דרישא, שאינו עושה בשבת איסור בידים — לא גזרו אי לאו דמיחייב חטאת; והיינו טעמא דאין נותנין עורות לעבדן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 17b:7:3.english: "One may not sell to a gentile" - Even though if [a Jew] were to perform these [actions] on Shabbat he would not be liable for a sin offering, nevertheless, since the gentile is driving [a laden animal] or performing by hand on Shabbat an action that a Jew is biblically forbidden [to perform], the Rabbis decreed [a restriction] at dusk, as explained in the Kuntres [Rashi], because he might be mistaken for his agent. However, in those matters of the opening section [of the Mishnah], where one does not perform a forbidden act by hand on Shabbat, they did not decree unless [doing so on Shabbat] entails liability for a sin offering; and that is the reason that [Beit Shammai ruled:] "One may not give hides to a tanner."

Tosafot on Shabbat 17b:7:4.hebrew: אין נותנין עורות לעבדן וב"ה מתירין - מכאן היה נראה לר"ת להתיר על ידי קבלנות נכרי לבנות בשבת. ועוד מביא ראיה מריחים דשרי ב"ה אליבא דרב יוסף בגמ', דמתירין להניח שם חיטין מבעוד יום ויניחנו כל השבת — כל שכן קבלנות על ידי נכרים דשרי. ואינו ראיה, דידעי כ"ע שהריחים טוחנות מעצמם, וידעי נמי שהחטין הושמו שם מע"ש; אבל קבלנות, יאמרו שצוה להם בשבת לעשות. ועוד מביא ראיה מסוף פ"ק דע"ז (דף כא: ושם), דאמר רשב"ג: "משכיר אדם שדהו לנכרי; מ"ט? אריס — אריסותיה קעביד". וה"נ קבלנותיה קעביד! ואף על גב דר"ש בן אלעזר פליג עליה, קיימא לן כרשב"ג, דסתם מתני' כוותיה. והא דאמרינן במ"ק (דף יב. ושם): "מקבלי קבולת — בתוך התחום אסור, חוץ לתחום מותר" — מוקי ר"ת התם כולה שמעתיה באבל, ולכך החמיר. ול"נ, דהתם איכא דמחמרי בחול המועד טפי מבאבל, ואפילו למאן דמחמרי טפי באבל מבחול המועד — מודה בשבת דחמיר טפי. ונראה לר"י, דהא דשרי בשמעתין עורות לעבדן, היינו בתלוש — דלא מפרסמא מילתא, שהנכרי עושה מלאכה בביתו, ולא ידעי שהוא של ישראל. וכן נמי אמר במ"ק (דף יא: ושם) גבי אבל: "מלאכתו ביד אחרים — בביתו לא יעשו, בבית אחרים יעשו". אבל קבלנות דמחובר, דהוי ברשות ישראל דמפרסמא מלתא — אסור בתוך התחום, דהרואה יאמר: "שכירי יום נינהו". והכי משמע בירושלמי דפירקין, דקאמר התם: אומני נכרים שהן עושים עם ישראל — בתוך ביתו אסור, בתוך ביתם מותר. אמר ר' שמעון בן אלעזר: בד"א? בקבולת, אבל בשכר אסור (פירוש: שכיר יום). בד"א? בתלוש, אבל במחובר אסור; ובעיר אחרת — בין בתלוש בין במחובר מותר. אמר ר"ש בר כהנא בשם רבי אחא: בשבת ובאבל ובע"ז הלכה כר"ש בן אלעזר. ורבינו תם נמי, כשבנה את ביתו, לא סמך על תשובתו ולא רצה להתיר. ומיהו בשדה מותר כרשב"ג, דבשדה רגילות לעשות באריסות ולא בשכירות יום. וכשישראל אומר לנכרי לתקן מנעלים או לקנות, אל יאמר: "תעשה למחר", דא"כ הוי כשכיר יום; אלא: "תעשה לכשתרצה". ואם הביא לו נכרי כליו ויודע שכבסן בשבת — אסור ללובשן בשבת, דאמר לקמן (שבת קכב.): נכרי שהדליק נר בשביל ישראל — אסור להשתמש לאורה. (תוספות ישנים):
Tosafot on Shabbat 17b:7:4.english: "One may not give skins to a tanner, and Beit Hillel permit" - From here, it seemed to Rabbeinu Tam to permit [a gentile] to build [a house for a Jew] on Shabbat by means of contracting [kablanut] with a gentile. And furthermore, he brings proof from [the case of the water]mill, which Beit Hillel permit according to Rav Yosef in the Gemara (below, 18a), where they permit placing wheat there while it is still day and leaving it [running] all through Shabbat; all the more so, contracting through gentiles should be permitted! But it is no proof, for everyone knows that the mill grinds by itself, and they also know that the wheat was placed there before Shabbat; but [regarding] contracting, [onlookers] will say that he commanded them on Shabbat to do [the work]. And furthermore, he brings proof from the end of the first chapter of Avodah Zarah (21b and there), where Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: "A person may lease out his field to a gentile. What is the reason? A sharecropper performs his own sharecropping [work]." And here too, [the contractor] performs his own contract work! And even though Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar disagrees with him, the halakhah is established according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, since the anonymous Mishnah is in accordance with his view. And as for that which we say in Moed Katan (12a and there): "For contractors [working on a Jew's building] — within the boundary [of the town] it is prohibited, [but] outside the boundary it is permitted" — Rabbeinu Tam establishes the entire discussion there as referring to a mourner, and therefore [the Sages] were stringent. But it does not seem [correct to us], for there [in Moed Katan], there are those who are more stringent regarding Chol HaMoed than regarding a mourner; and even according to the one who is more stringent regarding a mourner than regarding Chol HaMoed, he would agree regarding Shabbat, which is more stringent [than both]! And it appears to the Ri that that which is permitted in our sugya — [giving] skins to a tanner — is with detached items [talush], where the matter is not publicized, as the gentile performs the work in his own house, and [people] do not know that it belongs to an Israelite. And so too [the Gemara] says in Moed Katan (11b and there) regarding a mourner: "If his work is in the hands of others — in his house they may not do [it], but in another's house they may do [it]." But contracting on attached property [mechubar, i.e., real estate], which is in the domain of the Israelite, where the matter is publicized — it is prohibited within the boundary, for the onlooker will say: "They are day laborers!" And so it is implied in the Yerushalmi of our chapter, which states there: "Gentile artisans who work for an Israelite — inside his house it is prohibited, inside their house it is permitted. Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said: In what cases does this apply? With a contract [kablanut]; but for a [daily] wage it is prohibited" — explanation: [meaning] a day laborer. "In what cases does this apply? With detached property; but with attached property it is prohibited. And in another city — whether with detached or with attached property, it is permitted. Rabbi Shimon bar Kahana said in the name of Rabbi Acha: Regarding Shabbat, regarding a mourner, and regarding Avodah Zarah, the halakhah is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar." And Rabbeinu Tam himself, when he built his house, did not rely on his responsum and did not wish to permit [it]. However, regarding a field it is permitted in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, because in a field it is customary to work through sharecropping and not through day labor. And when an Israelite tells a gentile to repair shoes or to acquire [items], he should not say: "Do [it] tomorrow [on Shabbat]," for if so, it becomes like a day laborer; rather, [he should say:] "Do [it] whenever you wish." And if a gentile brought him his garments and he knows that he laundered them on Shabbat, it is prohibited to wear them on Shabbat, for [the Gemara] says later (Shabbat 122a): A gentile who lit a lamp for the sake of an Israelite — it is prohibited to use its light. (Tosafot Yeshanim)
